claim_formal: ∀ elliptic curve E/ℚ, ∀ prime q: s_q(E)∈{0,1} → (rank E(ℚ)=ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_q(E) ∧ #Ш(E/ℚ)<∞ ∧ L^{(r)}(E,1)/r! = Ω_E Reg_E #Ш ∏c_ℓ / #E(ℚ)_tors²)

quote_A.text: We prove the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one at some prime q.

quote_B.text: The rank and finiteness assertions are the unrestricted low-corank converse of \cite{C}; the two-primary leading-term equality is supplied by \cite{B}.

notes: BSD settled in Selmer corank ≤1 range only. Rank/finiteness and 2-primary parts come from companion OpenAI manuscripts (Selmer converse, two-primary BSD); this paper adds odd-prime valuations. Density-one twists corollary via result 006. M1 chosen for an equality between given quantities (could be read as M7). No Lean comparator.

claim_formal: ∀ Dirichlet character χ (incl. trivial, giving ζ), ∀ s∈ℂ with Re s>7/8, (χ,s)≠(principal,1): L(s,χ)≠0 (same for finite-order Hecke L-functions over ℚ(√-3))

quote_A.text: (hs : (7 / 8 : ℝ) < s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0 := by

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} resolves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis affirmatively

notes: Zero-free half-plane read as non-existence of zeros (M4); could also be read as a one-sided bound sup Re ρ ≤ 7/8 (M8) or M1 (property ¬L=0). Quasi-RH as posed is ∃σ0<1 ∀...; the explicit 7/8 makes it ∀. Corollaries: Vinogradov least-nonresidue conjecture, deterministic square roots, Landau–Siegel exclusion (separate manuscript), alternate 11/12 proof.

claim_formal: ¬∃ algorithm A ∀ n, ∀ f∈ℤ[X1..Xn]: A(f) halts and outputs [∃x∈ℚ^n f(x)=0]

quote_A.text: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial $f\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\Q^n$.

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers

notes: Closed statement about one decision problem. Second manuscript (pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational 2-torsion) is unrelated to the headline. No Lean comparator.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth compact connected Fujiki-class-C manifold X, ∀ rational SNC boundary Δ, ∀ fibration f:X→Y (connected fibres, Y normal compact): κ(X,K_X+Δ) ≥ κ(F,K_F+Δ_F) + κ(f|Δ), F very general fibre

quote_A.text: \kappa(X,K_X+\Delta) \geq\kappa(F,K_F+\Delta_F)+\kappa(f\mid\Delta).

quote_B.text: We prove Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for rational simple normal crossing boundaries on compact manifolds in Fujiki class $`\mathcal C`$, including coefficient one. Ordinary and logarithmic subadditivity follow.

notes: Headline = Campana orbifold subadditivity (stated for rational SNC boundaries; implies ordinary Iitaka C_{n,m}). Other manuscripts: Popa's log variation conjecture (κ̄(U)≥κ(F)+max{κ̄(V),Var f}), reverse log Kodaira inequality/additivity (stratum-smooth setting, O5-like), ordinary subadditivity via Hodge lines, Kähler b-semiampleness. Lean comparator (LogKodairaFiberNegative) formalizes the reverse log Kodaira inequality, not the headline.

notes: Companion manuscript: smooth projective surface whose universal cover is not holomorphically convex (disproves the conjecture in dimension two). No Lean comparator.

Zariski cancellation treated as an open question (P2); dimension 3 in char 0 remains open. Also disproves Stable Coordinate Conjecture (ambient dim 5) and Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture over A^1, A^2 (P1, O2).

notes: Kakeya maximal conjecture is posed in every dimension n; settled for n=3 (O5). Builds on Wang–Zahl 3D set theorem (GWZ set estimate). Second manuscript: 4D Hausdorff-dimension Kakeya conjecture (∀K⊂ℝ⁴ Kakeya: dim_H K=4; M9/M1, also O5). No Lean comparator.

claim_formal: ∀ f∈L log L(𝕋): for almost every x∈𝕋, S_N f(x) → f(x) as N→∞ (full sequence)

claim_formal: ∀ smooth nonnegative completely monotone g, ∀ locally finite C⊂ℝ² of centred-disk density one: E_g(C) ≥ Σ_{a∈A∖0} g(|a|²) = E_g(A), A the triangular lattice

notes: Minimality = lower bound attained by A, so M9 (could be read as M1 inequality). Problem: planar case of Cohn–Kumar universal optimality conjecture (Conj 9.4). Other manuscripts: Riesz 0<s<2 and Coulomb renormalized energy (Sandier–Serfaty conjecture, O1), 2D BHS log-energy constant, sharp Cohn–Elkies planar packing certificate (Cohn–Elkies Conj 7.3 in dim 2, ∃ f, M2).

claim_formal: ∀p∈(1,∞)∖{2}, ∀D>1 ∃C_{p,D} ∀n≥2: log n/log(1+2D) ≤ d_p(n,D) ≤ exp(C_{p,D}(log n)^{γ(p)}), so d_p(n,D)=n^{o(1)}; and d_p(n,1)=Θ(n²)

notes: Naor's question treated as an open question (P2), answered positively. Exact-distortion part (Θ(n²)) is a two-sided bound and secondary. Problem could be read as P3 if counted as a problem-list entry.

claim_formal: L = RL = BPL

quote_A.text: \[ \Lclass=\RL=\BPL. \]

quote_B.text: We prove $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving the derandomization problem for polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space.

notes: L=BPL is the standard derandomization conjecture (P1); could be P2. Secondary theorem: deterministic O(log n + q)-space approximation of acceptance probabilities.

claim_formal: ∀δ∈(0,1/3) ∃ deterministic poly-time reduction R_δ from 3-CNF φ to graphs G_φ: (φ sat → G_φ 3-colourable) ∧ (φ unsat → α(G_φ) < δ|V(G_φ)|); hence ∀ 3≤k≤c distinguishing k-colourable from non-c-colourable is NP-hard

quote_A.text: it is NP-hard to distinguish three-colorable graphs from graphs in which every independent set has fewer than δ times the number of vertices.

quote_B.text: The following consequence recovers the constant-palette hardness theorem.

notes: The intro says Fei–Minzer–Wang (4-to-1 games with perfect completeness) plus earlier reductions already resolve the constant-palette approximate-colouring conjecture; this family strengthens it to independent-set density with 3-colourable completeness. Hence O8. The OpenAI summary frames the headline as the c-colouring hardness (would be O1).

claim_formal: ω_ℂ ≤ 9/4, i.e. ∀ε>0 ∃C_ε ∀n: n×n complex matrices can be multiplied with ≤ C_ε n^{9/4+ε} arithmetic operations

quote_A.text: two $n\times n$ complex matrices can be multiplied using $O_\eps(n^{9/4+\eps})$ arithmetic operations. In particular, $\omega\leq9/4$.

quote_B.text: Dupont et al. report $\omega<2.371177$ by optimizing this combination-loss framework~\cite{Dup26}.

notes: Prefix 'none' reading ω≤9/4 as a closed statement about the constant ω; the operational form (and the Lean comparator) is ∀ε∃C∀n∃program. Other manuscripts: ω<2.258, α>0.465 in char 0; ω<2.371054886 over every field.

claim_formal: ∃ c>0, m0 (c=1/(5529600e), m0=1408) ∀ m≥m0: bdc(per_m) ≥ c m³ (hence dc(per_m) ≥ c m³)

quote_B.text: Mignon and Ressayre raised the exact lower bound to $\dc(\per_m)\ge m^2/2$ in characteristic zero

notes: Record improved from quadratic (Mignon–Ressayre) to cubic; the underlying VP vs VNP / superpolynomial dc conjecture is not settled. Explicit constants, so prefix could be '∀' (over m≥1408). Corollary: cubic lower bounds for ABP vertices/edges.

claim_formal: ∃ L∈P (deterministic TM, time C(n+1)^a) ∀A>0 ∃N_A ∀n≥N_A: S_3(f_n) > 2^{A√n}, f_n the n-bit membership function, S_3 = OR–AND–OR circuit size

quote_A.text: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 S_3(f_n)}{\sqrt n}=\infty. \]

quote_B.text: This is the depth-three lower-bound problem discussed by Gurumukhani, Paturi, Pudl\'ak, Saks, and Talebanfard~\cite[Section~1.1]{GPPST24} and still identified as open in~\cite[Section~1]{GKPRT26}.

notes: Treated as an open question answered affirmatively (P2/O1); alternatively P4/O7, since the stronger HJP95 question (2^{n^{1/2+ε}}) remains open. Prefix could be simplified to ∃∀^∞.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥1 ∃ B(d)<∞ ∀ real planar polynomial vector field V of degree ≤ d: #limit cycles(V) ≤ B(d)

quote_A.text: For each integer \(d\geq1\), there is a finite nonnegative integer \(B(d)\) such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most \(d\) has at most \(B(d)\) limit cycles in the whole plane.

quote_B.text: This establishes the uniform boundedness assertion in the second part of Hilbert's sixteenth problem.

notes: Hilbert's 16th (second part) is a problem-list entry (P3). It settles the uniform-boundedness ('existential Hilbert 16') assertion in full, but not the maximum number H(d), so O5 is a defensible alternative. 'ineffective': the paper says it gives no effective formula for B(d). Second manuscript: quintic Liénard systems have at most 2 limit cycles, sharp (Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh degree-5 case, M9, O5); the only Lean comparator (QuinticLienard) is for that result, not the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ finite IFS φ_i(x)=r_i x+t_i on ℝ with 0<|r_i|<1, ∀ positive probability vector p: dim_H μ_{Φ,p} = min{1, h_RW(Φ,p)/χ(Φ,p)}

quote_A.text: lowerHausdorffDimension μ = ENNReal.ofReal (min 1 (S.entropyRate / S.lyapunov))

quote_B.text: This resolves the entropy-rate dimension conjecture.

notes: An exact formula for the dimension (M9; M7 is possible). restricted_range = on the line (the conjecture's own setting). Corollaries: the no-exact-overlap formula and an attractor-dimension formula.

claim_formal: ¬∃ c:ℝ²→{1..5} with c(x)≠c(y) whenever |x−y|=1; hence 6 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7

quote_A.text: theorem no_proper_five_coloring : ¬ ∃ coloring : ℂ → Fin 5, ProperColoring 5 coloring

quote_B.text: This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.

notes: Lower bound on χ(ℝ²) improved from 5 (de Grey) to 6; Hadwiger–Nelson not settled, so O7. Problem could be labelled P2 (the H–N question itself) with the same O7. finite_checkable: by de Bruijn–Erdős (in ZFC) it is equivalent to the existence of a finite unit-distance graph with χ≥6, although the proof here is measure-theoretic.

claim_formal: ∃ (explicit) bipartite H on 35 vertices/66 edges ∃ finite simple graph G with an edge: t(H,G) < p(G)^66

quote_A.text: There is a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with at least one edge such that \[ t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}. \]

quote_B.text: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges

notes: H is explicit and G is shown to exist (not explicit). Corollaries: amplification (t(H,F)<c·p^66 for every c) and failure of the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture (also O2).

claim_formal: For uniform random triangle removal from K_n with terminal leave F_n: E[(F_n/n^{3/2} − 1/(2√2))²] → 0 as n→∞ (hence F_n/n^{3/2} → 1/(2√2) in probability and in mean)

quote_A.text: \frac{F_n}{n^{3/2}}\xrightarrow{\Prb}\frac1{2\sqrt2}

quote_B.text: This proves the triangle case of the sharp-constant conjecture of Joos and Kühn.

notes: Prefix is uncertain: a limit statement about one random process. Could be 'none' (closed statement about one process) or '∀^∞'. Joos–Kühn Conj 16.2 covers general strictly balanced hypergraphs and only the triangle case is settled, so O5. It also settles the Bollobás–Erdős n^{3/2} order with the sharp constant.

notes: Lean fixes H explicitly, so its prefix is ∀(c,C)∃(n,ε,A). Also answers Alon–Ben-Eliezer Problem 1.4 negatively (P3). Corollary: exp(Ω(ε^{-1/2})) query lower bound for canonical testers.

claim_formal: ∀ Borel probability law G on [0,∞) with no atoms and E[min(X1..X4)²]<∞: almost surely there is no bigeodesic in planar FPP on ℤ² with iid G-weights

quote_A.text: Then, with probability one, there is no sequence \((v_i)_{i\in\Z}\) of pairwise distinct vertices
